intelligence.human_view: He noticed it: remember that beautiful font we had from yesterday? How come it's just so plain today? We had incredible — that absolutely layered type font yesterday — but now it's not today. The eye notices the type before it notices anything else: yesterday the letters were layered and beautiful, today they are plain system type, and the whole page feels plainer for it. The font was found: Marcellus. The live walk still has it — it names Marcellus seven times. The staged free walk lost it when the fix round rebuilt it: only system sans and monospace, no Marcellus anywhere. That is why today is plain. A regeneration that drops the typeface drops the beauty with it — the fix round fixed the walk and unmade the look, and nobody noticed until his eye did. The fix rides in the follow-on round: restore the family and its loading from the live walk — harvest the type, don't re-pick it. And the lesson is bigger than one font: a rebuild must carry the beauty forward, not just the function. If the regenerated copy loses the type, the orbit, the palette, the feel — it is not the same page fixed, it is a plainer page that happens to work. The eye is the only check that catches that, because a mechanical check passes a plain page: the words are all there, the steps all work, and the beauty is gone.

They're called Marcellus, and they're still in the old page — we just have to bring them back!
